name: Belarus
summary_text: Belarus is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. In 2024 the authorities escalated from hostility to active persecution: a Culture Ministry decree reclassified transgender identity itself — "the desire to live and be seen by others as a person of an opposite sex" — as pornography, punishable by up to four years in prison. In September 2024 a wave of arrests targeted the community: TG House Belarus documented over 15 LGBTQ+ people detained, including at least eight transgender people, several arrested for merely subscribing to "extremist" resources online. Detained trans people were beaten and forced to record humiliating "confession videos" circulated on pro-government channels. ODIHR's 2024 reporting notes the majority of bias incidents in Belarus targeted trans people, including "physical assaults, threats, abductions, humiliation, and coerced confessions related to their gender identity by law enforcement officers." State media runs systematic dehumanising propaganda. Gender transition technically remains legal, but the 2024 pornography decree means a discoverable online presence or simply living visibly as trans can be prosecuted. For a visitor: no documented trans-tourist case yet, but police actively hunt trans people, any visible gender nonconformity risks detention, and foreign nationals receive no protection.

sources.title: Belarus Calls LGBT Lives ‘Pornography’ | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Apr 2024): 'Belarus Calls LGBT Lives 'Pornography'' — authorities treat depictions of LGBT life as banned 'pornography', extending repression of LGBT people.

sources.title: Belarus transgender rights organization says authorities detained over 15 LGBTQ+ individuals - JURIST - News
sources.claim_summary: JURIST (Sept 2024): TG House Belarus reported that 15+ LGBTQ individuals, including eight trans people, were detained within a month across several cities for allegedly subscribing to 'extremist resources'; most trans detainees were charged with hooliganism, two with pornography. Detainees reported physical and psychological abuse, and some fled the country. The Prosecutor General had announced in February a bill to punish 'promotion of non-traditional relationships'.

OSCE/ODIHR 2024 Hate Crime Report for Belarus: Belarus has not reported hate-crime data to ODIHR since 2015 and has no National Point of Contact; civil-society reports for 2024 came from Human Constanta and others. No official data available.
AP: 'Activists say police in Belarus beat LGBTQ+ people while arresting and charging them' — rights groups report beatings, coerced charges and expanding 'LGBT propaganda' repression.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Belarus: state TV equated LGBTI identities with paedophilia and called them 'a weapon in the hands of the West'; TG House recorded increased hate speech in state propaganda; the Prosecutor General's Office plans an administrative-penalty law against 'LGBTI propaganda' (not yet tabled); at least ten trans people left Belarus in a year due to discrimination and repression; a new National Security Concept emphasises 'traditional values'.

ILGA World Treaty Bodies Strategic Litigation Toolkit, Part 2 - Case Digest (2024): compilation of UN Treaty Body decisions on 25 SOGIESC cases (criminalisation, asylum, violence, expression, families, legal gender recognition) - includes jurisprudence relevant to Belarus among other states.

US State Department 1999 Human Rights Report for Belarus (archived): historical baseline - documents the legal and social situation including treatment of homosexuality under the Lukashenka government.

Report 'Are all equal before the law?' (Bortnik & Sementsov, citing Amnesty International 2006-2007 context): Belarus's constitutional equality guarantee (Article 22) versus reality - clampdown on civil society, harassment of activists, arbitrary detentions, death penalty retained; the legal and political climate facing LGBT people in Belarus.
